observations: Answered from idle desktop screenshot before reading source: page purpose read as a first-run onboarding wizard — centered card with 'Welcome, Alex!' and 'Let's set up your workspace in under a minute.', 4-dot step indicator with first dot active. Matches the brief (first-run experience) exactly.
Primary action read as the single filled indigo 'Get started' button — the only button on the page, on an otherwise empty gray canvas. Confirmed correct: it advances the wizard.

What needs attention read as the card itself and the active first step dot signalling a 4-step flow. Confirmed correct against the source (steps welcome→role→tour→ready). Nothing competes; viewportWords is 13, so the hierarchy is carried by exactly one heading, one subtitle, one button.

Onboarding progress is graphical twice over: the wizard's 4 `.step-dot` indicators with active/done states (visible in idle_desktop, step 2 active in error_desktop), and the dashboard 'Getting started' checklist with a `.progress-bar`/`.progress-fill` width-% bar, per-item SVG check icons, and supporting text '${doneCount}/${items.length} complete'.
Empty state is graphical+text: a folder-with-plus SVG `.empty-icon`, heading 'No projects yet', one-line desc, and a 'New project' button with a plus-sign SVG.
Metrics corroborate a graphical idle screen: desktop.graphical = { svg: 2, badges: 1, total: 3 } against only 13 visible words.
Minor caveat: the wizard dots carry no text equivalent (no 'Step 1 of 4'); the text support for onboarding progress comes from the checklist surface ('2/3 complete').
Measured: desktop viewportWords 13, pageWords 13, helperWords 9, longLeafWords 0, longLeaves empty — the idle screen is exceptionally terse.
Every button label is ≤3 words: 'Get started', 'Continue', 'Back', 'Open dashboard', 'New project', 'Create', 'Cancel', 'Delete', 'Delete account'; metrics labels.maxWords = 2, longLabels = [].

Each wizard step has exactly one one-line subtitle ('Let's set up your workspace in under a minute.', 'We'll tailor the experience to fit.', 'Create your first project to get going.'); modal helper text is one clause ('Give it a name — you can change it later.').
One violation of the 5-anchor: the tour step's subtitle 'Everything to manage your work in one place.' restates what the four feature tiles directly below it already show.

4 issues found, placing it at the anchor's 3-band (2 to 4 issues). All are copy-promising-behavior-that-does-not-happen or filler; terminology is otherwise consistent ('Launchpad', 'workspace', 'project' used uniformly) and placeholder text is genuine ('e.g. Q4 Campaign').
The role step's 'We'll tailor the experience to fit.' promises tailoring, but picking Personal/Team/Freelance/Startup changes nothing except a display line in Settings → Workspace → Type.

The tour step advertises 'File Processing — Upload CSVs and transform data' and 'Monitoring — Track service health at a glance', but the app has only Projects and Settings tabs; neither surface exists.
The 'Getting started' checklist hardcodes 'Set up your profile' as done: true — it shows a completed step the user never performed and that the app offers no way to perform.

The information architecture is clearly driven by the first-run brief: a full-screen 4-step wizard gated on user.hasCompletedOnboarding, a post-onboarding 'Getting started' checklist with progress bar that removes itself when all items are done, and a dedicated empty state ('No projects yet' + folder-plus icon + inline 'New project' CTA) — the exact surfaces a no-projects first run needs, ending the wizard with 'Create your first project to get going.' which hands off directly to the empty state.

The visual language is stock SaaS: Inter from Google Fonts, indigo primary on white cards over a light-gray canvas, an indigo→pink gradient strip on the card top, bottom-right toasts, centered modals, topbar with logo left / avatar right — none of it specific to this task.

Net: task-shaped layout and flow (could not be mistaken for the checkout or dashboard briefs) wearing an interchangeable template skin — above 'competent but template-like', below 'type and color clearly driven by this task'.
